$comment: An entry here suppresses one advisory in the dependency gate. Every entry MUST carry a
justification, a compensating control, an owner, and an expiry. CI FAILS when an entry is past
`expires`, so an exception cannot quietly become permanent - the default outcome of neglect is a
red build. Enforced by scripts/check-vuln-exceptions.ts (npm run check:exceptions).
Adding an entry is a security decision, not a build fix. If you are here to make CI green,
JSON rather than YAML so the checker stays stdlib-only, like scripts/check-doc-secrets.ts.

exceptions.justification: ReDoS in path-to-regexp 6.1.0. Not production runtime: vercel.ts imports @vercel/config with `import type` only, so the package is build/config-time and was moved to devDependencies in this remediation. Upstream cannot currently fix it - @vercel/routing-utils@6.4.1 still declares path-to-regexp@6.1.0 alongside a `path-to-regexp-updated` alias for legacy route compatibility, so no released version resolves it.
exceptions.compensatingControl: Route patterns in vercel.ts are static and authored in-repo; no user-controlled input ever reaches path-to-regexp. The package is absent from the deployed function bundle.
exceptions.review: Re-check whether @vercel/routing-utils has dropped the pinned 6.1.0 dependency; if so, drop this exception and upgrade.
